---
title: "Upgrading across a format change"
description: "What to do when a release changes the on-disk format: delete the cache with every worker stopped, or give each format its own directory for a rolling deploy, and what happens to sessions, counters and queues."
---

You bump diskcache-oxide in `requirements.txt`, deploy, and the app won't start: opening the cache raises `FormatMismatchError`. Or, with a `Caches` registry, it starts and the log fills with the error while every request runs uncached. The new release stores its data differently, and it won't read a database written the old way. For a cache that's a cold start and nothing more, as long as you know which directories to delete and which data in them wasn't really cache.

## Which releases need this

Before 1.0, a release that changes the on-disk format bumps the minor version and says so first in its [changelog](https://github.com/mikeckennedy/diskcache-oxide/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) entry. The last number goes up with every release, a minor bump included, so 0.1.2 is followed by 0.2.3. A release that keeps the format needs nothing: install it and restart.

0.2.3 is a format change. It adds tags and the eviction policy to the database (format 3), so a cache made by 0.1.2 can't be opened by 0.2.3, and 0.1.2 refuses a cache made by 0.2.3 the same way. Neither version reads or changes anything in the other's database. Opening the other version's cache raises `FormatMismatchError`, naming the file:

```text
FormatMismatchError: cache format version 2 is not supported (this build uses version 3) (in /var/cache/my-app/diskcache-oxide.sqlite): it was made by an older diskcache-oxide: delete the cache's directory (a FanoutCache's whole root) with every process using it stopped, and it will be recreated empty
```

A [`Caches`](../user-guide/caches.qmd) registry doesn't raise. It logs the error at `ERROR` on the `diskcache_oxide` logger (or passes it to your `on_open_error`), hands out a `NullCache` so requests carry on uncached, and tries to open the directory again every `retry_open_after` seconds (10 by default). Once you've deleted the old directory, the next retry creates a fresh cache and caching comes back without a restart.

## The simple path: stop, delete, start

If you can stop every worker for a moment, this is all there is to it:

1. Stop every process that uses the cache: web workers, Celery workers, cron jobs, a REPL someone left open.
2. Delete the cache's directory. For a `FanoutCache`, delete the whole root, never one shard: a shard deleted alone would be re-created next to shards still in the old format.
3. Deploy the new release and start the workers. The directory is re-created empty on the first open.

```bash
systemctl stop my-app my-app-worker
rm -rf /var/cache/my-app
pip install --upgrade diskcache-oxide
systemctl start my-app my-app-worker
```

Delete the directory, not just `diskcache-oxide.sqlite`: values of 64 KiB or more live in files beside the database, and they'd be left behind. With a `Caches` registry, each registered cache is a directory under the base directory (unless you gave it `directory=`), so deleting the base directory clears them all.

If a 0.1.2 worker is still running when you delete its cache and 0.2.3 re-creates it, the old worker can't damage the new database. Its writes go to the deleted file through the connections it already holds, and once it opens the new file, its writes, deletes and maintenance calls fail with "no such table" (only `touch` gets through). Stop every worker before deleting anyway: this only keeps a straggler from doing harm.

## Rolling deploys: one directory per format

A rolling deploy runs old and new workers side by side for a while, and they can't share a cache across a format change. Give each minor version its own directory, so new workers start on an empty one while old workers finish on theirs. A directory named after the first two parts of `diskcache_oxide.__version__` changes exactly when the format can:

```{python}
import diskcache_oxide

def format_series(version: str = diskcache_oxide.__version__) -> str:
    major, minor = version.split('.')[:2]
    return f'v{major}.{minor}'

print('this build:', diskcache_oxide.__version__, '->', format_series())
print('0.1.2 ->', format_series('0.1.2'), '| 0.2.3 ->', format_series('0.2.3'))
```

Use it wherever the app opens its caches:

```python
from diskcache_oxide import Caches

caches = Caches(f'/var/cache/my-app/{format_series()}', timeout=1.0)
caches.register('general')
caches.register('pages', size_limit=2 * 2**30)
```

A release that only bumps the last number (0.2.3 to a later 0.2 release) keeps the same directory and keeps its cache. A minor bump starts cold even on the rare occasion it doesn't change the format, which is a small price for never having to check.

After the deploy, once every old worker has stopped, delete the directories the old versions used. Run this from the deploy script, or from a job [one worker claims](run-once.qmd):

```python
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

def remove_old_caches(root: str = '/var/cache/my-app') -> None:
    keep = format_series()
    for path in Path(root).glob('v*'):
        if path.is_dir() and path.name != keep:
            shutil.rmtree(path)
```

A rollback works either way. If the old directory is gone, the old version re-creates it empty. If it's still there, the old version opens it as it was left, and nothing the new version deleted while it ran ever reached it, so values without an `expire` may be stale. Delete it before rolling back unless every entry expires soon.

The first time you adopt this pattern, the old workers' cache is wherever they had it before, and that's the directory to delete once they're gone. If they used a plain `Cache` at `/var/cache/my-app`, that directory is itself a cache, so put the versioned directories under another root (`/var/cache/my-app-caches/v0.2`) instead of inside it. A `Caches` base directory isn't a cache itself, so `v0.2/` can sit beside the old registry's cache directories.

### While both versions run

For the length of the overlap, old and new workers each have a cache the other can't see:

- **Invalidation reaches one side only.** A worker that deletes a key after a database update deletes it from its own version's cache. The other side keeps serving the old value until it expires. Keep the overlap short, and keep an `expire` on cached values, so it can't last long.
- **Coordination splits in two.** A [job claim](run-once.qmd) made on one side doesn't stop the other, so a scheduled job can run once per version. A [rate limit](rate-limiting.qmd) counts each side separately, so a client can get up to twice its limit. Locks and semaphores from the [Coordination](../user-guide/coordination.qmd) guide don't exclude workers on the other version.

If any of that is a problem for your app, use the simple path instead.

## State that isn't really cache

A cache entry can be rebuilt from somewhere else. Some of what apps keep in a cache directory can't be, and deleting the directory for a format change loses it. Deal with each kind before you upgrade:

- **[Work queues](work-queues.qmd).** Items still queued are lost. Stop pushing new work, let the workers drain the queue until `peek(prefix=...)` returns `(None, None)`, then upgrade. With one directory per format, old workers can drain the old queue while new producers fill the new one; check that the old queue is empty before deleting its directory.
- **[Counters](counters.qmd).** Counts since the last flush are lost. Run the flush job once more with the old release, after its last worker stops and before you delete the directory. If that isn't practical, a once-a-minute flush loses under a minute of counts.
- **[Sessions](sessions.qmd).** Everyone is logged out. Upgrade at a quiet hour, or tell users ahead of time. During a rolling deploy with one directory per format, a user who lands on a new worker looks logged out, and after signing in again can bounce back to an old worker where that session doesn't exist. An app that keeps sessions in the cache is better served by the simple path.
- **[Job claims](run-once.qmd), rate limits and [single-use keys](single-use-keys.qmd).** These expire on their own anyway. After the upgrade, a claimed job may run again and a client's rate limit starts over. A one-time token issued before the upgrade stops working, so a password reset link from just before the deploy has to be requested again.

## Things to know

- **Settings stored in the cache go with it.** `size_limit`, `cull_limit` and `eviction_policy` are stored in the database. The new cache takes them from the constructor, or the defaults. A value you changed at runtime with `reset()` has to be set again, so pass it to the constructor or to `register()` instead.
- **A cache made by a newer release** raises `FormatMismatchError` too, saying it was made by a newer diskcache-oxide. That's an old worker meeting a new cache: upgrade it, or point it at another directory.
- **It's always safe to start cold.** Deleting a cache's directory with every worker stopped loses what was in it and nothing else. If a cache is ever in doubt, that's the fix. See [Errors and what to do about them](../user-guide/errors.qmd#formatmismatcherror-a-database-this-version-cant-read).
